name: ExaUser
follows_en: Partial, vendor says robots.txt rules may not apply to user-initiated fetches

ips.note: The vendor says every request is signed with Web Bot Auth (RFC 9421) and publishes its keys at a public directory; it does not publish an IP list.

vendor_quote: Exa uses ExaUser to fetch a page live when a user, or an application built on the Exa API, asks for its current content.
what_en: ExaUser is the agent Exa uses to fetch a page live when a user, or an application built on the Exa API, asks for its current content. Exa says it is not used to crawl the web automatically; that is ExaSearchBot. It does not try to bypass logins, paywalls or CAPTCHAs, and submits no forms.
block_en: Exa says that because fetches are initiated by a user, robots.txt rules may not apply to ExaUser. It also says ExaUser is not used to decide whether content appears in Exa search, and that search opt-outs and automatic crawling are managed with the ExaSearchBot token in robots.txt.
compare_en: ExaSearchBot crawls automatically to build Exa's search index and follows robots.txt, while ExaUser fetches a page only when a user or application asks and the vendor says robots.txt may not apply.
notes: Key directory not fetched; no IP list published. The vendor page names no robots.txt token for ExaUser beyond the name itself; token = ExaUser is the name it uses.
answer_en: ExaUser is the agent Exa uses to fetch a page live when a user, or an application built on the Exa API, asks for its current content. Exa says robots.txt rules may not apply to such user-initiated fetches. Search opt-outs and automatic crawling are controlled with the ExaSearchBot token instead.
